citeAs: Wadhawan, R., Bansal, H., Chang, K.-W., and Peng, N. (2024). CONTEXTUAL: Evaluating Context-Sensitive Text-Rich Visual Reasoning in Large Multimodal Models. Proceedings of the 41st International Conference on Machine Learning, Vienna, Austria. PMLR 235.
creator: Rohan Wadhawan, Hritik Bansal, Kai-Wei Chang, Nanyun Peng (University of California Los Angeles)
description: CONTEXTUAL is a context-sensitive text-rich visual reasoning dataset consisting of 506 challenging instructions for large multimodal model (LMM) evaluation. It covers eight real-world visual scenarios (time reading, shopping, navigation, abstract scenes, mobile application, webpages, infographics, and miscellaneous natural scenes) with human-crafted instruction-response pairs that require joint reasoning over embedded text and visual context in images.
name: CONTEXTUAL
rai:annotationsPerItem: For human evaluation: each model response was rated by 3 independent human annotators; final decision by majority vote. For dataset verification: MTurk workers verified each sample's correctness.
rai:annotatorDemographics: Primary annotators were the paper authors (researchers at UCLA). Human performance baseline annotators and human evaluators were sourced from Amazon Mechanical Turk, mainly from the US. MTurk workers who passed a qualification test were selected for human performance baseline collection.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: MTurk workers verified 96% of samples as correctly annotated in Stage 3. For human evaluation, majority vote among three annotators was used as the final decision. Correlation analysis between human and automatic evaluation metrics was performed using ROC-AUC and Spearman correlation; GPT-4 evaluation achieved the highest ROC-AUC of 85.9 and Spearman correlation of 0.71 with human judgments.
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Amazon Mechanical Turk (MTurk) for verification (Stage 3) and human performance baseline collection; paper authors performed primary annotation (Stage 2)
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Three-stage annotation process: Stage 1 — image shortlisting via manual filtering (for Time, Shopping, Navigation, Abstract) or heuristic-based filtering using PaddleOCR to select top 500 images with highest word count (for Application Usage, Web Usage, Infographic, Miscellaneous Natural Scenes). Stage 2 — authors divided into two groups, each annotating four categories following strict annotation guidelines to create instruction-response pairs requiring context-sensitive reasoning (not solvable by OCR alone). Stage 3 — MTurk workers verified correctness of each sample; 96% were annotated correctly; incorrect samples were filtered; each author group then reviewed the other group's samples for quality and guideline adherence, resulting in 506 final instances.
rai:dataBiases: Human annotators for the baseline were mainly from the US, which may introduce linguistic and cultural bias in human responses and evaluations. The authors acknowledge that linguistic diversity and writing style would change with different social groups. The dataset avoids instructions solvable by OCR alone to prevent text-reading bias. Open models may underperform on digital scenes due to training data predominantly comprising natural scenes (e.g., COCO dataset).
rai:dataCollection: Images were sourced from six different sources: (1) LAION-5B via CLIP-retrieval UI keyword search for Time, Shopping, Navigation, and Abstract categories; (2) Rico Dataset (66,000 UI screens from 9,300 Android apps) for Application Usage; (3) screenshots scraped from Open WebText Initiative website links for Web Usage; (4) InfographicVQA dataset for Infographic; (5) STVQA and ESTVQA datasets for Miscellaneous Natural Scenes. Human-written instruction-response pairs were then annotated for each image by the paper authors in a three-stage process.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Images sourced from LAION-5B (via CLIP-retrieval UI keyword search), Rico Dataset (Android UI screenshots), Open WebText Initiative (web screenshots), InfographicVQA dataset, STVQA dataset, and ESTVQA dataset. These were then annotated with novel human-written instruction-response pairs requiring context-sensitive reasoning.
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Web Scraping, Manual Human Curator
rai:dataLimitations: Human annotators were mainly from the US, limiting linguistic and cultural diversity of human baseline responses and evaluations. The dataset is a fixed benchmark of 506 instances, which may not cover all possible visual contexts. Synthetic data generation for context-sensitive text-rich visual reasoning is challenging; automatically generated instructions tend to be solvable by OCR+LLM rather than requiring true context-sensitive reasoning. The dataset does not test all possible real-world scenarios requiring joint text-visual reasoning.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For Time, Shopping, Navigation, and Abstract categories: manual filtering of images for suitability. For Application Usage, Web Usage, Infographic, and Miscellaneous Natural Scenes: heuristic-based filtering using PaddleOCR to detect text and select top 500 images with the highest number of words. Images from existing VQA datasets (InfographicVQA, STVQA, ESTVQA) were re-annotated with novel context-sensitive instruction-response pairs. A validation set of 100 samples (30 from Miscellaneous Natural Scenes, 10 from each other category) was split out, with reference responses hidden for the remaining 406 samples.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is released with a validation set of 100 samples (with reference responses) and 406 samples with hidden reference responses. A continuously updated leaderboard is maintained on HuggingFace. The dataset, code, and leaderboard are available on the project page.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is designed to evaluate LMMs on context-sensitive text-rich visual reasoning, with real-world applications including assisting the visually impaired in navigating text-rich scenes. The authors ensured images, instructions, and responses are not offensive to any social group. The authors acknowledge that existing multimodal models can generate harmful responses despite safeguard filters, and that hallucinations were observed in model responses (though no apparent harmful or privacy-sensitive information was found). The authors note that human annotators were mainly from the US, and linguistic diversity and writing style of responses would vary across social groups; future work should involve annotators from more diverse regions.
rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking and evaluating large multimodal models' capability on context-sensitive text-rich visual reasoning. Intended use cases include assessing model performance on real-world tasks such as navigating public spaces, interpreting text-rich scenes for assisting the visually impaired, and creative understanding of abstract text-rich images (e.g., memes). Also intended to inspire development of next-generation LMMs with improved visual perception and reasoning.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: PaddleOCR (PP-OCRv4 model) used for heuristic-based image filtering (selecting top 500 images with highest word count) and for extracting OCR from images in experiments. CLIP-retrieval UI used for keyword-based image search from LAION-5B. ShareGPT-4V-7B used for generating dense image captions in augmented LLM experiments. GPT-4V used for synthetic data generation pipeline.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The authors state that no apparent harmful or privacy-sensitive information was observed in model responses during qualitative analysis. The dataset images were collected from public sources (LAION-5B, Rico Dataset, Open WebText, existing VQA datasets) and the authors aimed to ensure images and annotations are not offensive to any social group.
